Are you a customer-obsessed builder with a passion for helping enterprises transform how work gets done? Amazon Quick is the AI assistant built for work — turning questions into answers, answers into actions, and actions into outcomes — and we need a GTM leader who can take that vision to every enterprise in EMEA. Do you combine deep domain expertise in enterprise productivity with the business acumen to land transformation programmes tied to real customer outcomes? Do you thrive at the intersection of technology strategy and commercial execution?
Join the EMEA Go-to-Market Specialist Team to grow Amazon Quick adoption across some of the most exciting businesses in the market.This is a Principal-level GTM Specialist role that will design and execute use-case-led motions across sales, finance, marketing, HR, legal, and IT that land measurable business outcomes.

The Worldwide Specialist Organization (WWSO) is part of AWS Sales, Marketing, and Global Services (SMGS). We work backwards from our customers' most complex and business-critical problems to build and execute go-to-market plans that turn AWS ideas into multi-billion-dollar businesses. WWSO teams include business development, specialist solutions architecture, and go-to-market.

This is a Principal-level GenAI GTM Specialist role responsible for driving enterprise Generative AI adoption across EMEA. Rather than owning a single service, you will own the cross-cutting GenAI transformation narrative — spanning Amazon Bedrock, agentic architectures, foundation model strategy, and emerging GenAI capabilities — and translate it into use-case-led motions that land measurable business outcomes in customers.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the EMEA GTM strategy for Amazon Quick — driving enterprise adoption through use-case-led motions that show how Amazon Quick adds value for customers
• Develop and execute account-level strategies for customer success, guiding organizations from proof-of-concept to production and value creation at scale.
• Operate at the CxO/VP and practitioner level — engage senior business leaders on how Amazon Quick transforms the way their organisation works, while simultaneously working with IT leaders, developers, and architects on enterprise deployment best practices.
• Build and execute scaled GTM programmes — design motions including customer roundtables, use-case workshops, and regional campaigns that create awareness and accelerate adoption of Amazon Quick.
• Thought Leadership — create packaged deliverables and drive enablement that raises the bar across the EMEA field.
• Be the voice of EMEA customers to Product — synthesise regional customer requirements and emerging agentic patterns into actionable feedback that shapes the Amazon Quick roadmap.

What We’re Looking For

• Deep domain expertise in enterprise business productivity, collaboration, or SaaS platforms — with demonstrable understanding of how AI is transforming knowledge work, content creation and business intelligence.
• Demonstrated ability to land AI or digital transformation programmes in enterprise customers — translating technology capability into business outcomes by use case.
• A blend of technical depth and commercial acumen — equally comfortable articulating how agentic workflows, and enterprise AI assistants work while presenting a productivity transformation strategy to a C-suite.
• Experience building and executing GTM strategies at scale in a fast-moving technology domain, ideally in business productivity, collaboration tools, or enterprise SaaS.
• Data-driven approach to prioritisation — using pipeline data, propensity signals, and market intelligence to focus effort where it matters most.
• Experience in enterprise technology sales, solutions architecture, or technical business development with a focus on productivity platforms, AI/ML, or cloud services.

A day in the life
You will lead the go-to-market strategy for Amazon Quick. You might start your morning on a deep-dive with an Enterprise customer mapping their enterprise-wide AI rollout strategy — showing how Quick’s knowledge graph learns each employee’s priorities, preferences, and network to deliver deeply personalised assistance across sales, finance, marketing, and operations. After lunch, you’re running a use-case workshop with a major Retailer’s IT leadership, helping them see how Amazon Quick can connect to data sources, help them build interactive dashboards, and automate workflows and building the business case to take to their board.
Later, you’re jumping into a pipeline review with a sales leader to understand how to support opportunities that are ready to move from pilot to production. You’ll collaborate daily with account teams, solution architects, customer success managers, and AWS service teams — connecting the dots between customer business priorities, Amazon Quick’s capabilities, and market opportunity. Your job is to make the complex simple: translating the art of the possible in AI-powered work into concrete, transformation programmes that customers can execute and measure.

About the team
The EMEA WWSO AI/ML Geo Specialist team within AWS’s Worldwide Specialist Organization owns and executes go-to-market strategy for the full portfolio of AWS AI/ML services. We serve customers across the complete AI lifecycle while also leading the way to drive net new innovative use cases in this domain. Our customers include some of the most technically sophisticated organizations in the world, and our work directly impacts how AI is built and deployed across EMEA.

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. About the Role

We’re looking for a Rack Power Engineer with deep expertise in high-power conversion and distribution to design, qualify, and support power systems for AI supercomputers. You will own rack power solutions—including power shelves, AC/DC rectifiers, power supply units (PSUs), power management controllers (PMCs), and high-current distribution—from requirements and supplier development through deployment. You will also monitor fleet rack power health, lead debugging and root-cause investigations, and drive improvements into hardware, firmware, and qualification coverage.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

- Own rack power architecture and requirements for high-power AI supercomputing systems, including power budgets, AC input interfaces, DC distribution, redundancy, efficiency, serviceability, and integration with data center infrastructure.

- Drive the design and supplier development of power shelves, rectifiers, PSUs, PMCs, busbars, connectors, and protection circuits. Review electrical designs and control behavior, and evaluate performance, cost, reliability, and availability trade-offs.

- Define and execute component, shelf, and rack qualification plans covering load transients, current sharing, hot-swap, startup and shutdown, redundancy failover, fault protection and recovery, thermal limits, and AC disturbances and ride-through.

- Partner with firmware and software teams to define and validate PMC functionality, telemetry, alarms, power sequencing, power capping, and fault handling. Verify communication interfaces, firmware updates, interoperability, and regression coverage.

- Characterize rack power under representative AI workloads. Translate steady-state demand and fast power excursions into design margins, protection settings, energy-storage needs, and deployment requirements with system and data center teams.

- Establish fleet rack power health metrics with operations teams. Analyze telemetry, event logs, and failure trends to detect degraded power capacity, redundancy loss, current imbalance, and recurring power faults.

- Lead lab and fleet debugging across power hardware, firmware, and system interfaces. Reproduce failures, identify root causes with suppliers, validate corrective actions, and feed lessons into designs, qualification tests, and fleet remediation.

- Work with electrical, mechanical, thermal, firmware, manufacturing, reliability, and data center teams to take rack power systems through prototype builds, qualification, production, and deployment. Drive supplier test reviews, manufacturing test coverage, and closure of power-related issues.

- Evaluate emerging rack power technologies, including higher-voltage DC distribution and battery or supercapacitor energy storage. Partner with suppliers to qualify viable solutions and with safety and compliance teams to address applicable product requirements.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have at least 10 years of industry experience in power electronics or power delivery systems, including hands-on design and qualification of high-power rack or data center power systems.

- Have a master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Have strong knowledge of AC/DC rectifiers, power shelves, PSUs, and DC distribution, including three-phase inputs, power conversion topologies, control-loop stability, current sharing, redundancy, protection coordination, and high-current busbars and connectors.

- Have experience defining and qualifying PMCs or related power controllers, including telemetry, fault management, hardware–firmware integration, and interfaces such as PMBus, I²C, CAN, or Ethernet. Understand how rack power controls interact with system power management.

- Have strong laboratory and debugging skills using oscilloscopes, power analyzers, programmable AC sources, electronic loads, and data acquisition systems. Can build automated tests, analyze fleet telemetry with tools such as Python, and drive root-cause investigations through verified corrective actions.

- Have taken power products from requirements through qualification and production with suppliers and cross-functional teams. Bring familiarity with safety, EMC, and reliability qualification; communicate technical trade-offs clearly; and work effectively through ambiguity. Experience with high-density AI racks, OCP power architectures, or energy-storage systems is a plus.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role

The Detection & Response (D&R) team plays a critical role in protecting our systems, users, and data from security threats. We’re looking for an experienced Technical Program Manager to own and evolve incident management within D&R. This is a senior-level specialization on the Technical Program Manager ladder, focused on how we detect, respond to, and learn from security and operational incidents.

You’ll be the driving force behind maturing and scaling our incident response lifecycle—from detection and triage through containment, remediation, and post-incident review. Critically, some of the highest-impact work in this role happens after the immediate response: gathering data on incident trends, reporting on patterns and root causes, and working cross-functionally across engineering, security, infrastructure, and product teams to ensure that broad fixes and systemic improvements are actually implemented.

You won’t just manage incidents—you’ll make sure we get meaningfully better after each one.

Responsibilities

• Own the end-to-end D&R incident management program: detection workflows, response processes, escalation paths, communication standards, and remediation tracking.
• Serve as incident commander for security incidents, driving clear coordination across executive, engineering, security, legal, and other appropriate stakeholders.
• Establish and run incident commander rotations within D&R, ensuring clear ownership and effective coordination during incidents of varying severity.
• Drive post-incident accountability by defining how action items are captured, assigned, tracked, and completed across teams—ensuring follow-through on both tactical fixes and strategic improvements.
• Gather, analyze, and report on incident trends and patterns to surface systemic risks, recurring root causes, and areas where the organization is most vulnerable.
• Translate trend analysis into actionable cross-functional initiatives: partner with engineering, infrastructure, security, and product teams to prioritize and implement broad fixes and preventive improvements that address root causes rather than symptoms.
• Lead incident review forums (post-mortems, retrospectives) and ensure learnings are captured, socialized, and acted upon across the organization.
• Develop and maintain D&R incident response documentation, playbooks, runbooks, and training materials; keep them current as the threat landscape and our systems evolve.
• Partner with detection engineering to improve alert fidelity, reduce noise, and shorten time-to-detection for security events.
• Define, develop, and track incident management KPIs and report regularly to D&R and Security leadership.
• Support broad cross-functional training and initiatives to uplevel security awareness across the company (e.g. Tabletop exercises, training, talks).

You may be a good fit if you:

• Have 7+ years of experience in technical program management, incident management, or security operations, with significant time spent in a detection & response or security incident response context.
• Have led or built incident response programs at a technology company, ideally in a high-growth or security-intensive environment.
• Have a demonstrated track record of turning incident data into organizational improvements—not just writing post-mortems, but driving the cross-functional work to implement systemic fixes.
• Are comfortable participating in on-call responsibilities and leading incident response during high-severity security events, including off-hours.
• Have experience building and scaling operational processes from the ground up in environments where structure didn’t previously exist.
• Excel at driving accountability and follow-through across multiple teams without direct authority—you know how to influence, track, and close the loop.
• Have strong analytical skills and experience with incident trend analysis, metrics reporting, and data-driven prioritization.
• Are highly organized with a knack for bringing structure to ambiguous, fast-moving situations.
• Have excellent communication skills, especially under pressure and when coordinating across technical and non-technical stakeholders, including executive leadership.
• Thrive in fast-paced environments where priorities shift and you’re often working with incomplete information.

Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$290,000—$365,000 USD

Logistics

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. The Regional Higher Ed Lead is the single point of ownership for AWS Academy within an assigned geographic territory. This role is accountable for growing and managing a portfolio of higher education institutions advising on technical curriculum and cloud/AI strategy and serving as the trusted advisor connecting institutions to the right combination of AWS education programs. You will own the institutional relationship end-to-end - from pipeline development through onboarding through long-term account health - while defining the technical standards and requirements that ensure institutions successfully implement and deliver Academy courses. You will work across AWS teams (sales public sector partner organizations curriculum and platform engineering) to bring coordinated value to higher education institutions in your region. Key job responsibilities • Institution Pipeline & Business Development Identify prospect and onboard new institutions into AWS Academy. Build and manage a pipeline of prospective institutions from inquiry through active enrollment. Grow adoption within existing accounts by expanding program presence into new departments and degree programs. Coordinate with AWS Sales field teams on Academy opportunities and identify areas of collaboration with public sector public policy and partner organizations to create scalability. • Account Management & Relationship Ownership Serve as the primary point of contact for all institutions within the territory. Drive retention expansion and educator readiness across assigned accounts. Build long-term relationships with institutional stakeholders - department chairs deans and provost-level leadership. Shepherd dormant institutions back to active status. Ensure educator nominations and readiness-to-teach milestones are met. Track regional KPIs including learner completions institution growth and educator engagement. • Technical Advisory & Curriculum Strategy Advise institutions and educators on AWS cloud and AI curriculum architecture course sequencing and how Academy programs map to degree requirements. Communicate technical training standards and curriculum development best practices to institutional partners. Understand and articulate technical aspects of LMS integration (LTI protocols Canvas configuration SSO/SAML) lab environment requirements (Vocareum AWS Labs) and platform capabilities. Define technical requirements for institution setup and ensure institutions can successfully deploy and deliver Academy courses. • Program Execution & Cross-Functional Coordination Execute global business development and event playbooks locally - including AWS Jams hackathons and vibe coding sessions. Coordinate with the Technical Enablement Lead on content standards and educator readiness requirements. Work with the Business Development & Strategy Lead on go-to-market motions and marketing activities in-region. Advocate internally for institutional needs across AWS teams. Connect institutions to the right combination of AWS programs - Academy Education Equity Initiative Cloud Clubs Skills to Jobs - based on institutional needs. In the afternoon you sync with Sales on a joint opportunity align with the Technical Enablement Lead on educator readiness and plan an in-region AWS Jam.
